title: LMCache: Remote code execution via unsafe deserialization in multiprocess mode transport (CVE-2026-105192)
description: LMCache versions from 0.3.9 up to but not including 0.5.6 have a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in multiprocess mode via unsafe pickle deserialization on the ZeroMQ transport port (default 5555). The transport socket, used for inter-process communication, lacks authentication and deserializes attacker-controlled data using pickle.loads, allowing arbitrary code execution as the LMCache process user. By default, the transport binds to localhost, but multi-node deployments often bind to routable addresses, exposing the service. Official container images run the LMCache process as root, increasing risk. The vulnerability is fixed in version 0.5.6 by replacing pickle with a safe, versioned MessagePack format and restricting network exposure.
aiSummary: LMCache's multiprocess mode opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER socket (default port 5555) for worker processes to share cache blocks. This socket accepts msgpack messages that include an extension type deserialized via pickle.loads without authentication, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability affects versions from 0.3.9 through 0.5.5 and 0.5.6 release candidates prior to the final 0.5.6 release. The default configuration binds to localhost, but multi-node setups often bind to 0.0.0.0 or other routable addresses, exposing the service to network attackers. The official container images run the LMCache process as root, so exploitation leads to root code execution. The issue is fixed in 0.5.6 by removing pickle deserialization, implementing a typed MessagePack allowlist, changing the wire format, binding example deployments to localhost, and running containers as non-root users.
aiImpact: An attacker who can connect to the ZeroMQ transport port (default 5555) on a vulnerable LMCache deployment can send a single crafted message that triggers unsafe pickle deserialization, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the LMCache process. Since official containers run LMCache as root, this can lead to full system compromise. Single-host default installs binding only to localhost are not exposed remotely, but multi-node or misconfigured deployments binding to routable addresses are vulnerable. The vulnerability has a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8 (critical).
